Create GitHub issue for staff review Abstract Whitespace errors are common to digitized archives.
This paper describes a lightweight unsupervised technique for recovering the original whitespace.
Our approach is based on count statistics from Google n-grams, which are converted into a likelihood ratio test computed from interpolated trigram and bigram probabilities.
To evaluate this approach, we annotate a small corpus of whitespace errors in a digitized corpus of newspapers from the 19th century United States.
